builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: English Calibration Erodes Lithuanian in Expert-Pruned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
summary: It replaces the common practice of pruning MoE experts with a single English calibration set by calibrating with Lithuanian or mixed Lithuanian-English data before REAP pruning. The cost is obtaining a representative target-language calibration set and running the pruning and evaluation once per language served, with no required increase in deployed model size. It can fail if the served language concentrates routing in a few late-layer experts that an English-only calibration marks unimportant, causing disproportionate target-language degradation.
rationale: For a small production team using MoE compression, matching the calibration language to the deployment language is a low-infrastructure change that directly avoids the documented multilingual quality collapse.
technique: Language-matched calibration for MoE expert pruning

claims.statement: It replaces the common practice of pruning MoE experts with a single English calibration set by calibrating with Lithuanian or mixed Lithuanian-English data before REAP pruning. The cost is obtaining a representative target-language calibration set and running the pruning and evaluation once per language served, with no required increase in deployed model size. It can fail if the served language concentrates routing in a few late-layer experts that an English-only calibration marks unimportant, causing disproportionate target-language degradation.

At 25% pruning with English calibration, Lithuanian comprehension fell by a median of 21.4 points versus 1.7 for English; Lithuanian or mixed calibration removed most of that loss and was about 2.5 points better for English comprehension than English calibration.
